item.title: European countries agree to set up migrant 'return hubs' outside EU
item.description: EU countries on Monday backed a significant tightening of Europe's immigration policy, including endorsing the concept of setting up "return hubs" outside the 27-nation bloc for failed asylum-seekers.

item.title: TELL US: Americans in Europe, would you give up US citizenship to be European?
item.description: After a US Senator sparked uproar by introducing a bill that would eliminate the possibility of dual citizenship for American citizens, we want to hear from US nationals in Europe. Would you give up your US passport to be European?

item.title: Your views: 'There is so much wealth in Sweden’s diversity'
item.description: Comments by readers of The Local Sweden – whether opinions, advice or tales of life in the country – offer vital insights to others. We've picked out some recent contributions on topics spanning loneliness, tougher rhetoric towards migrants and things readers miss from home.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Tuesday
item.description: Avanza outage makes it look like savings have vanished, bad weather stops 'Christmas tree flyover', and other news from Sweden on Tuesday.

item.title: LONG READ: In Sweden, there are only good, bad, ugly and evil immigrants
item.description: Drawing on his own experiences, Faisal Khan examines how Swedish society sorts immigrants into four familiar stereotypes — the good, the bad, the ugly and the evil immigrant. The solution, he argues, is for Swedes and immigrants to meet more often.

item.title: When to spot the Swedish Air Force's flying Christmas tree?
item.description: Is it a bird? Is it a plane? Make sure to look up on Wednesday: you might just catch sight of an airborne Christmas tree.

item.title: Sweden acquits activists who smeared paint on Monet painting
item.description: A Swedish court on Monday freed six environmental activists involved in a climate protest where they smeared red paint on the protective glass of a Monet painting, saying they had not intended to harm the artwork itself.

item.title: Swedish pro-government parties 'agreed on a plan' for second term in power
item.description: Sweden's four pro-government parties have "agreed on a plan" for their second term in power at a cosy meeting at the Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's house, which also involved Christmas presents and tasteless festive jumpers.

item.title: UN slams Sweden's 'discriminatory' push to tighten citizenship rules
item.description: A UN committee has sharply criticised immigration reforms pushed through by Sweden's government, arguing that plans to tighten citizenship requirements were "discriminatory", while stop-and-search zones were "illegal".

item.title: Swedish word of the day: wallenbergare
item.description: Today’s word is a Swedish dish thought to be based on the Swedish equivalent to the Rockefellers.
